jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Digital Education and Empowerment for Patients with Atrial Fibrillation and Comorbidities
jobs.description:
At the Faculty of Medicine, Department of Health Science and Technology a postdoc in digital education and empowerment for patients with atrial fibrillation and comorbidities are available for appointment from January 1, 2027, or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

The Department of Health Science and Technology (HST) at Aalborg University is an interdisciplinary research and teaching environment where engineering, medicine and health sciences come together to improve people's lives.

As a postdoc at HST, you will be affiliated to the Section of Public Health at the Department of Health Science and Technology and become part of an international research community with access to experienced supervisors, modern research facilities and strong interdisciplinary collaboration. You will work alongside researchers from a wide range of disciplines and engage with hospitals, industry and public-sector partners to address some of society's most important health challenges.

The department is home to approximately 180 academic staff members, around 100 PhD fellows and more than 1,700 students. We offer a stimulating research environment that encourages scientific curiosity, collaboration and professional development.

At HST, our values – Share. Care. Dare. – shape the way we collaborate, support one another and create knowledge with societal impact.

Learn more about the department on our website and in our research portal.

**Your work tasks

**The postdoc will be affiliated with the research and innovation project AF-EMPOWER: Digital Education and Empowerment for Patients with Atrial Fibrillation (AF) and Comorbidities. AF is one of the most common cardiovascular diseases, is frequently associated with comorbidities such as hypertension, heart failure, obesity, diabetes, and sleep disorders, and AF prevalence is expected to double over the next two decades. Education is a cornerstone of AF care, supporting patient engagement and self-management, yet many patients still report insufficient understanding of their condition and its management. The psychological impact of AF and its comorbidities is increasingly recognized as an important aspect of care. The aim of the AF-EMPOWER study is to co-design, develop, test and evaluate a tailored digital educational and empowerment application for patients with AF and comorbidities and relatives to assess its feasibility, effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness compared with usual care.

The postdoc will coordinate and contribute to the co-design process, prototype and program development, feasibility test and evaluation of the effectiveness of the AF-EMPOWER application. You will be involved in data collection, data analysis, and dissemination of research findings. The project combines perspectives from systemic innovation, psychosocial well-being, digital health literacy and equity, behavioural science and patient empowerment, implementation science and mixed-methods evaluation.

The Postdoc will work closely with patients with AF, their relatives, healthcare professionals from the Department of Cardiology and the Department of Citizens’ Health at the Regional Hospital in Viborg and Silkeborg, as well as municipalities, general practitioners (GP), community organizations, and researchers. The position requires the ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks, apply for funding and collaborate confidently and effectively with a diverse range of stakeholders.

Applicants should have:

• A master’s degree and a Phd in health sciences, physiotherapy, nursing, sociology, psychology, or social sciences

• An interest in co-design, interdisciplinary collaboration, and digital technologies

• Well-developed skills in conducting research, analyzing data and disseminating results

• Collaborative competencies to work in an interdisciplinary context

• A demonstrated track record of securing research funding

• Language skills in Danish and English (oral and written)

• Access to a car

Qualification requirements Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, outlining your motivation for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications if relevant.

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

In your cover letter, please explain why you find AF-EMPOWER interesting, how your research background can contribute to the project, and which methodological and research skills you would bring to the project.

We look forward to receiving your application.

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

The position is subject to a three-month probationary period applicable to both parties.

Aalborg University – Knowledge for the World

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer programmes grounded in real-world challenges and produce world-class research through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private organizations. These collaborations generate insights, new solutions to societal challenges, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, with additional campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Principal Scientist, Analytical Development, you'll use your extensive experience in the analysis of synthetic therapeutics, including peptides and oligonucleotides, to serve as the analytical lead supporting our synthetics programs from first-in-human through commercial readiness.

You will support both early- and late-stage development, including phase-appropriate method validations and Quality Control activities, setting and justifying specifications, process and product characterization, and preparation of CMC regulatory submissions, including NDAs and MAAs. You will drive analytical strategies and manage analytical activities across multiple CROs and CDMOs, helping to ensure smooth progression from clinical manufacturing to commercial readiness.

What you'll do

• Own analytical strategy for synthetics programs, particularly peptides and oligonucleotides, from first-in-human through commercial readiness.

• Establish phase-appropriate analytical approaches, including setting and justifying specifications, product characterization, impurity marker synthesis and qualification, reference standards, stability protocols, comparability assessments and risk assessments.

• Provide technical input to CDMOs on method development and validation (especially for purity methods), as well as product characterization.

• Manage analytical method transfer, optimization and validation with external partners, including in support of commercial readiness.

• If appropriate, ensure an appropriate mechanism of action-based potency assay is in place to support Phase 3 readiness.

• Provide analytical expertise on CMC sub-teams, working closely with Drug Substance, Drug Product, Research, Quality and Regulatory colleagues.

• Provide analytical support for process characterization, including determination of Critical Quality Attributes and appropriate validation of methods for testing In-Process Controls.

• Lead and manage analytical CROs/CDMOs, material suppliers, consultants, vendors and collaborators; monitor regulatory trends, integrate new analytical approaches, identify opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs, and advise colleagues on data interpretation.

• Author and review analytical sections of regulatory submissions, from first-in-human through NDAs and MAAs, and represent Hemab as an analytical expert in regulatory interactions when needed.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Proven industry experience setting analytical strategy for synthetic therapeutics, particularly peptides and oligonucleotides, with substantial exposure to late-stage development through commercialization.

• Strong working knowledge of phase-appropriate analytical method development and validations, setting and justifying specifications, product characterization, impurity marker synthesis and qualification, comparability assessments and regulatory submissions, especially NDAs/MAAs supporting late-stage synthetic programs.

• Significant experience managing CROs/CDMOs, including navigating technical problems where an external partner needs hands-on guidance.

• Strong understanding of ICH expectations for stability and method validation, together with experience producing analytical content for regulatory submissions.

• Flexibility, a proactive approach and comfort operating in a fast-paced biotech environment spanning multiple time zones.

• A relevant scientific degree, with a PhD preferred, and the technical depth to operate as an independent analytical expert.

Nice to have

• Experience with mechanism of action-based potency assays.

• Experience establishing reference standards.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. You will likely build some of your own tools and processes instead of inheriting finished products. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

This position spans early- and late-stage development and works across multiple internal teams, CROs, CDMOs, suppliers, consultants, vendors and collaborators. Hemab operates across multiple time zones.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

We are seeking an early-career RF Engineer to contribute to the design, development and validation of RF communication subsystems for nanosatellite missions.

In this role, you will support RF analysis and integration activities across UHF, VHF, S-band and X-band systems, perform link-budget analyses and help validate performance through hardware-in-the-loop and over-the-air testing.

You will join our Satellite Systems Hardware team in Aalborg and collaborate closely with colleagues across RF, Hardware, and Systems Engineering. Your Role

As RF Engineer, you will support the development and validation of RF subsystems for satellite missions, from link-budget analysis and RF-chain modelling through integration, hardware-in-the-loop testing and over-the-air validation.

Working with experienced engineers, you will gradually build the knowledge and practical experience needed to take responsibility for increasingly complex RF engineering tasks.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Support RF subsystem analysis and technical trade-offs across frequency bands, performance and mission constraints.

• Perform link-budget analysis and RF-chain modelling.

• Contribute to the definition and documentation of RF subsystem requirements and interfaces.

• Support the integration, verification and validation of RF subsystems, including hardware-in-the-loop and over-the-air testing.

• Assist with the evaluation and selection of RF front-end components across UHF, VHF, S-band and X-band.

• Prepare and carry out laboratory measurements using RF test equipment.

• Analyse test results and contribute to troubleshooting RF performance issues.

• Contribute to onboard signal-processing and data-reduction activities for RF applications.

• Document analyses, test activities and technical conclusions clearly and systematically.

• Provide technical input to mission proposals with support from experienced colleagues.

What Success Looks Like

In the initial phase, success means:

• Understanding GomSpace’s NanoCom product portfolio and SDR architecture.

• Building effective working relationships with colleagues across RF, Hardware and Systems Engineering.

• Completing a link-budget analysis for an active mission with guidance from experienced colleagues.

• Performing your first hardware-in-the-loop or over-the-air RF test using GomSpace equipment.

• Documenting your analysis and test results in a clear and structured way.

• Communicating RF results and technical observations clearly to colleagues from other disciplines.

Over time, you will take increasing responsibility for RF subsystem analysis, integration and verification activities. You will contribute independently to mission proposals and projects while helping develop reusable RF models, test methods and engineering tools.

What You Bring

You are a recent graduate or early-career RF engineer who is motivated to apply your technical knowledge to real satellite systems. You enjoy combining analytical work with practical laboratory activities and want to develop your skills within an experienced multidisciplinary team.

You likely bring:

• An MSc in Electrical Engineering, RF or Microwave Engineering, Telecommunications or a related field.

• Up to one year of relevant experience in RF engineering, communication systems, testing or integration.

• A basic understanding of RF engineering principles and communication systems.

• Experience with RF analysis, simulation or laboratory measurements gained through your studies, thesis, student employment, internship or first professional role.

• Familiarity with RF simulation or engineering tools such as CST, ADS, HFSS, MATLAB, Python or similar.

• Some experience with RF test equipment, such as spectrum analysers, vector network analysers or signal generators.

• An interest in satellite communication systems, software-defined radio or digital signal processing.

• Good analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Good written and spoken English.

Experience from the space or aerospace industry is an advantage but is not required. Relevant academic projects, thesis work, internships and student positions will also be considered.

Knowledge of modulation schemes, communication protocols, RF payloads, ECSS standards or space-grade RF qualification would be beneficial.

Who You Are

You are curious, systematic and motivated by the opportunity to turn engineering analysis into working hardware. You enjoy learning from experienced colleagues while also taking responsibility for your own tasks and development.

You are known for:

• Technical curiosity – eager to understand how RF systems perform in practice.

• Attention to detail – careful when analysing results, conducting tests and documenting conclusions.

• Hands-on problem solving – interested in moving between simulation tools and the laboratory bench.

• Collaborative communication – comfortable working with RF, systems, payload and hardware engineers.

• Structured execution – able to plan your work, follow up on tasks and communicate when support is needed.

• Customer focus – understanding that good engineering contributes directly to the success of our customers’ missions.

• Willingness to grow – open to feedback and motivated to build deeper RF subsystem expertise.

Why Join Us

You will have the opportunity to begin or develop your RF engineering career by working on communication systems for real nanosatellite missions.

The position offers hands-on experience across RF analysis, laboratory testing and system-level integration. You will work with flight-proven NanoCom radios and SDR platforms while learning from experienced specialists across RF, Hardware, and Systems Engineering.

Your work will contribute to mission proposals, subsystem development and technologies that ultimately fly in space. As your experience develops, you will take on increasing technical responsibility and have the opportunity to shape the tools and methods used by the team.

Join our mission

jobs.occupation: Tenure track Assistant professor/Associate professor Position in Materials Science and Engineering
jobs.description:
Aarhus University, Denmark

The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering at Aarhus University invites applications for two positions at the rank of:

•   Tenure Track Assistant Professor, or

•   Associate Professor

The positions are offered within the broad field of Materials Engineering and Manufacturing, with a particular focus on participating in the department’s research and education in materials engineering, durability, emerging and advanced materials, advanced manufacturing and surface engineering. The department seeks candidates who will help shape a modern materials science profile, in research as well as in teaching, and who have demonstrated relevant experience in the field.

Expected start date

July 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible.

Research Areas

We welcome applicants with a solid background in materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, materials-focused chemical engineering, applied physics, or closely related disciplines.

We particularly encourage applications within, but not limited to, the following research themes:

Additive and hybrid manufacturing

Including metal additive manufacturing, laser-based processing and welding, joining of metallic and dissimilar materials, post-processing, surface engineering, and process characterisation and modelling.

Materials durability and advanced materials

Including materials under demanding and extreme conditions, 4D printing, bioprinting, and biofabrication, surface modification, lubrication technologies and functional surfaces.

Applicants are expected to contribute to both fundamental understanding and applied solutions, with relevance to engineering systems and industrial applications

Research and Teaching Responsibilities

The selected candidates will:

•   Teach, contribute to, and develop courses in materials science and engineering, additive manufacturing, and manufacturing processes at different levels, from foundational bachelor’s courses to specialized master’s and PhD courses

•   Contribute directly to the further development of the materials and manufacturing science curriculum at different program levels

•   Supervise bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD students

•   Attract external research funding

•   Engage in knowledge exchange with industry and research partners

•   Participate in departmental and university service activities

Your Profile

We are looking for candidates who can contribute to research, education, and innovation at an international level.

To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:

-   A PhD in materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, or a closely related field

-   Substantial experience conducting high-quality research in materials science and engineering, with publications in leading international journals that match career stage

-   Experience in at least one of the research areas listed above, along with familiarity with experimental, computational, or theoretical research methods

-   Interest in interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering disciplines and with industry

-   For the positions as associate professor, the applicants should, in addition, have:

-   Documented teaching experience and a clear commitment to teaching and advancing materials science courses, from introductory undergraduate instruction through master’s and PhD-level study

-   For associate professor applicants: a documented record of self-directed research leadership, external funding acquisition, supervision of PhD students, and teaching and course development at university level

Who we are

The engineering field in Aarhus University is evolving with a rapid growth in student population, major research initiatives as well as through the establishment of a number of new physical facilities in the city center of Aarhus. We have comprehensive plans for increased activities in research and education, as well as public and industrial cooperation. The  Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering  within the Faculty of Technical Sciences has cooperation with universities and advisory service providers in more than 20 countries. The engineering field at Aarhus University is well established with extensive research activities, over 700 mechanical engineering students and a long tradition of industrial cooperation that we wish to extend significantly.

What we offer

The department offers:

-   research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

-   an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

-   a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

-   a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

-   a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance

Place of work and area of employment

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Mechanical and Production Engineering, Katrinebjergvej 89, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contact information

For more information about the position contact Head of Section of Manufacturing and Mechatronics, Professor Ramin Aghababaei (ra@mpe.au.dk / +45 9350 8956)

or Head of Section of Mechanics and Materials, Professor Michal Kazimierz Budzik (mibu@mpe.au.dk, +45 4189 3217)

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than December 8th, 2026.

Technical Sciences Tenure Track

Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship.

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level

• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists

• to create transparency in the academic career path

As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure

• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training

• a mentoring programme

• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level

As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The Department of Environmental Science at Aarhus University, Roskilde, Denmark, invites applications for a permanent position as Associate Professor in Environmental Chemistry. We seek a motivated and collaborative researcher who will contribute to improving and expanding our internationally recognised research and research-based advisory and teaching activities within environmental chemistry and related disciplines. The position is available from April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a permanent position starting April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
The Department of Environmental Science at Aarhus University aims to expand and diversify its research, teaching, and advisory activities addressing current and future environmental challenges. We are therefore seeking an Associate Professor in Environmental Chemistry to contribute to the continued development of the Section for Environmental Chemistry and Toxicology.

The candidate is expected to establish and maintain a research profile while contributing to collaborative research activities across the department and with external partners. The position offers considerable freedom to develop new research directions within environmental chemistry and related disciplines under the responsibility to keep your group including yourself mainly externally funded.

The Associate Professor will contribute to:
 * Development of an internationally strong and externally funded research programme. 
 * Research addressing the occurrence, fate, transport, transformation, exposure, and impacts of chemical contaminants in natural and engineered systems. 
 * Research-based advisory activities for Danish ministries, public authorities, and other stakeholders. 
 * Teaching and course development at Life Long education, MSc, and PhD levels. 
 * Supervision of MSc students, PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and other junior researchers. 
 * Development of interdisciplinary collaborations across environmental chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, biotechnology, modelling, and data science. 
 * Knowledge exchange and collaboration with governmental agencies, industry partners, and international research networks.

The selected candidate is expected to contribute directly to both basic and applied research and to support the department's longstanding tradition of combining scientific excellence with societal impact through research-based advisory services

Your profile
Applicants hold a PhD in Environmental Chemistry or a closely related discipline.

The selected candidate should have documented research experience within at least one area of environmental chemistry and demonstrate the ability to develop an internationally visible research profile.

Particular emphasis will be placed on:
 * Scientific productivity documented through publications in international peer-reviewed journals. 
 * Ability to develop and maintain national and international research collaborations. 
 * Experience in obtaining external research funding, or clear potential to do so. 
 * Experience with university teaching and supervision. 
 * Effective communication and collaboration skills. 
 * Commitment to contributing to an inclusive and collegial research environment.

In addition, experience within the following areas will be considered:
 * Development and application of analytical methods for trace analysis of organic contaminants in environmental and biological matrices.
 * High-resolution mass spectrometry, including target, suspect screening, or non-target workflows.
 * Environmental fate, transport, and transformation of organic contaminants.
 * Environmental monitoring programmes and environmental assessment.
 * Exposure assessment and chemical risk assessment.
 * Environmental data analysis, chemometrics, or environmental data science.
 * Research-based advisory activities, including experience supporting governmental authorities or regulatory agencies.
 * Experience with the Danish environmental advisory system or similar national or international regulatory frameworks.
 * Interdisciplinary research bridging environmental chemistry with toxicology, ecotoxicology, microbiology, biotechnology, engineering, or computational sciences.

Qualifications at the Associate Professor level will be assessed in accordance with the criteria specified in the Danish university job structure and Aarhus University's assessment criteria for permanent academic positions.

Who we are
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University. The knowledge base encompasses fields such as social science, geography, economics, and policy analysis, in addition to mathematical modeling, physics, chemistry, toxicology, and microbiology. Both pure and applied research is conducted on some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution and pollution control mechanisms, management of land, soil, water, air and biodiversity, protection of ecosystem services and climate change. Research based advisory services within these areas are offered to ministries and other stakeholders and central to the Department economy. Currently, about 150 staff and PhD-students are working at the department. Further information may be found at http://www.envs.au.dk.

The selected candidate will be affiliated with the Section for Environmental Chemistry and Toxicology. The section conducts research and research-based advisory work targeting a better understanding of the transport and fate of organic pollutants in the environment, as well as a better understanding of the links between environmental chemistry, toxicology and human exposure. This includes tools to identify and quantify impacts, which can act as indicators of emerging problems. The aim is to provide the highest capability in Denmark for assessing risks associated with the distribution and fate of organic pollutants in the environment.

What we offer 
The department and section offer:
● An active, internationally recognised research environment
● a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories with high-end analytical equipment
● an interdisciplinary environment with both national and international collaborators as well as authorities and private companies
● a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
● a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
● a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work will be at Aarhus University, RISØ Campus, in Roskilde, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark. The city of Roskilde (www.roskilde.dk) is located close to Copenhagen. The area provides immediate access to a wealth of cultural and recreational pursuits.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Head of Section, Pedro Carvalho, +45 8715 8462, pedro.carvalho@envs.au.dk or Head of Department, Carsten Suhr Jacobsen, +45 2537 7667, csj@envs.au.dk. 

Technical Sciences Tenure Track
Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship. 

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level
• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists
• to create transparency in the academic career path
As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure
• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training
• a mentoring programme
• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level
As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation. 

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.
